stem: Build the rectangle with sides $x + {=a}$ and $x - 4$ from algebra tiles (negative tiles are hatched and marked −). The tiles that fill it are the expansion of $(x + {=a})(x - 4)$.
solution: Anchor the single $x^2$ tile. It is $x \times x$, the product of the two $x$ terms.
Along the top edge, lay one positive $x$ tile for each unit added to $x$ in the first bracket. Together they are $x \times (\text{that number})$.
Down the left edge, lay four negative $x$ tiles (hatched, marked −), one for each unit in $-4$. Together they are $x \times (-4)$.
Fill the block that the two runs bound with unit tiles. Each unit is positive times negative, so every unit tile is negative.

Read the rectangle. Positive and negative $x$ tiles cancel in pairs. The four negative ones outnumber the positive ones, so the $x$ term is $(\text{number} - 4)x$, which is negative whenever the number is less than 4. The expansion is $x^2$, plus the net $x$ tiles, plus the unit tiles.
notes: Parent is (d-4)^2 (ex1-11-22c); this is the same factor x-4 with the other number left free (k = -4 gives the book's question). The three own misconceptions on this objective come from asking when the x coefficient of (x+k)(x-4) is positive, and all three predict a POSITIVE x term for k = 1, 2, 3, whereas the tiles show it is negative (-3x, -2x, -x). So the build refutes 'any positive k makes b positive' and 'k below 4 makes b positive' directly. Why only middle-term-sign is mapped: giving the two runs the opposite signs (-k on top, +4 down the side) is a valid rectangle with the right constant -4k and a flipped x term (4-k)x, which is exactly the predicate's description and exactly the reversal 'kx - 4x read as 4 - k'. Not mapped: (1) x-term-from-k-alone (leaves the -4x tiles out): dropping a run leaves a gap, which would fire not-a-rectangle, and that predicate also fires for a stray tile, so it does not diagnose this one error. When both signs are flipped the student lands on middle-term-sign, and the likelier error there is the reversal. For a = 2 'k alone' and 'reversed' give the same wrong x term (+2x). (2) x-term-taken-from-constant-product concerns reading b off the constant -4k, which the tile build does not exercise. (3) constant-sign, missing-cross-term and off-target have no own misconception to name. Instrument limits: |a|, |b| <= 4 and b is fixed at -4, so the net x term never exceeds 0 here; the 'b is positive when k > 4' half of the original question cannot be built with this widget. a = 4 is left out on purpose: the x tiles cancel to nothing, so a student who skips the cross term is right by accident, and a sign reversal also gives 0.
